thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 streaming latency spike detected (eu-west) — SSE/WebSocket stalls increasing across several frontends. Auto-page to eng-oncall.

alice: Paging eng-oncall @dave — p99 jumped to ~3.8s for streaming tail on /v1/stream, customers reporting partial responses. Ticket created INC-1234. :rotating_light:

dave: On it. grabbing logs and checking proxy timeouts first. any customer-facing impact noted?

support-bot: FYI: 3 inbound customer reports in last 5m referencing stalled streams, one paying account (acct-889). Added to INC-1234.

carol: Querying metrics — origin servers look healthy, backend tokenization p50 stable. Proxy write queue depth up on eu-proxy-7. p95 for proxy write is 1.9s, p99 3.6s.

ben: Repro attempt shows SSE chunk gaps ~10-15s between chunks under certain body sizes. curl shows socket open but no data for a while.

alice: Stack trace / logs snippet from frontend: ```
2026-03-17T09:54:12Z frontend[euw-3] WARN chunk-write timeout after 15000ms to client 10.0.2.45
2026-03-17T09:54:13Z proxy[euw-7] INFO backlog=187 write_retries=3
```

dave: Hypothesis: client backpressure + proxy TCP write stall causing long tail. Will check kernel socket stats and keepalive timers. If proxy write buffer stuck, try rotating traffic off eu-proxy-7.

carol: Adding runbook step: temporarily reroute streaming traffic for eu-west to fallback pool in another AZ, enable shorter proxy write timeout (from 20s -> 8s) to drop stuck connections faster.

dave: Executing failover: `infractl route modify --from eu-west --to eu-west-b` (will monitor). Starting with canary 5% then 50%.

ben: Noted a side effect: some clients (longpoll fallbacks) may reconnect more frequently — watch for reconnection storms.

alice: Communications: support, please prepare an update for paying customers impacted with ETA for mitigation.

support-bot: Draft prepared and posted to INC-1234. Customer acct-889 informed about mitigation steps; they acknowledged.

dave: Canary at 5% applied. Observing metrics... p99 reduced to ~2.1s in canary slice. Queue depth on eu-proxy-7 down 60%.

carol: Good signal. Rolling to 50% now. Also enabling prefix/KV cache for common prompts to reduce token generation spikes.

alice: Will we need a rolling restart of eu-proxy-7? Might be safer after traffic shift.

dave: Plan: finish reroute -> drain eu-proxy-7 -> rolling restart with netstat + tcpdump capture for postmortem.

ben: Also adding temporary rate limit for streaming endpoints at the edge: `X-Stream-Rate-Limit: 6r/s` for high-throughput clients to reduce pressure while we stabilize.

support-bot: Customer update sent: "We've applied a mitigation by shifting traffic and expect improved latency within 10-15m. We're monitoring and will update."

alice: Monitoring shows p99 back to baseline ~0.9s across eu after full reroute. Marking immediate customer impact as mitigated.

dave: Started drain + restart on eu-proxy-7; capturing `ss -tin` and `tcpdump -w /tmp/proxy7.pcap` for RCA.

carol: Postmortem notes to include: proxy write buffer tuning, default keepalive/timers, edge rate-limits, and a test for client backpressure behavior under high chunk frequency.

alice: Oncall handoff: @oncall-rotation please continue watch for 4h, follow runbook steps in INC-1234, escalate to SRE if p99 >2s again.

oncall-rotation: Ack — taking handoff. Will keep an eye on reconnection rates and customer tickets.

alice: Thanks team. Closing incident channel once postmortem draft added to INC-1234. :white_check_mark:
